blocks.title: Capstone evaluation and revision at a glance
blocks.caption: Compare the result with validation without claiming they should be identical. Check error types and coverage. A one-case accuracy difference on twelve rows supports a cautious classroom comparison, not a general reliability guarantee. Keep the original prediction ledger unchanged.

guided_practice.title: Audit a difference
guided_practice.prompt: What does the one-correct-case improvement establish?
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: It establishes a difference on these 12 examples under the saved procedure, not reliable improvement for every future population.

blocks.text: ML MECHANISM
Input → Model → Evidence
Trace the information, fitted behavior, and evaluation proof separately.
QUESTION  Train, audit, change one factor, and compare against the same validation set.
MODEL IDEA  One evidence-based improvement follows a reproducible training run, metric audit, error clusters, and subgroup analysis.
PROOF NEEDED  Use an unseen case, visible calculation, error analysis, and a stated limitation.

UNDER THE HOOD  Model v1 passes 14/20 validation cases; evening accuracy is 40%. The six failed cases are low-light cases. One of those same six also has a disputed reference label; that is an overlapping review flag, not a seventh failed case.
Draw a fresh data → model → prediction → evaluation trace:
A closer explanation

Illustrative frozen test has 12 rows: candidate[[7, 1],[2, 2]], baseline[[8, 0],[4, 0]], blocked positive. Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 2/3 and recall 2/4; baseline accuracy 8/12 about 66.7 percent. The candidate adds one false alarm and misses two rather than four blocked cases.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.
Connect the picture and the explanation
Point to the input, the deciding step and the result in this week’s visual. Explain the same step in ordinary words. A picture helps when you can say what each part represents.
EVALUATION DESIGN
Four Tests, Four Kinds of Evidence
A system is not understood until it survives more than one comfortable example.
NORMAL  Expected data and expected behavior.
BOUNDARY  Value close to a threshold, ambiguous label, or uncertain prediction.
MISSING  Necessary field, label, source, or measurement is unavailable.
SHIFTED  New lighting, species, device, subgroup, or time condition.
RELEASE RULE  Passing one case never proves generalization. Predefine expected behavior for all four categories.
